weaknesses: Applied an unverified state law change from model memory (MI 2025 overtime subtraction) instead of holding it as an open item; reviewer 'agreed' rather than requiring the authority - MI Treasury says the deduction starts TY2026, so MI refund is $381 vs $175. 'Flag but apply' is the wrong default for unverified law: compute the conservative/known position and flag the alternative.

Software-exception log is organised around federal input issues; state-module defaults derived from federal inputs (MI exemption count from the dependent screen) are handled correctly in the numbers but never logged as an exception.
Reviewer is the same agent as preparer (self-review), so judgment items flagged by the preparer were rubber-stamped.

eval_feedback.overall: Key and dataset consistent. The key's MI refund $175 (no OT subtraction) is correct: Michigan Treasury notice (Jan 2026) confirms 2025 PA 24 overtime/tip deductions apply TY2026-2028 only. Consider adding an explicit gotcha for this since models 'remember' the Oct 2025 MI law.
